## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The replace path still works as it did before. The new adopt branch records a change and rewrites the file even when the incoming value already matches the stored one. That breaks the module's promise to preserve untouched configuration files. No other defects found.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/config.py:13 — correctness — The `elif adopt:` branch assigns the value and calls `changes.append(key)` without checking `current[key] != value`, unlike the replace branch at app/config.py:19. Take a file containing `{"theme":"dark"}\n` and call `merge(path, {"theme": "dark"}, adopt=True)`: it returns `["theme"]` and rewrites the file as `{\n  "theme": "dark"\n}\n`. Could you guard the adopt branch with the same `if current[key] != value:` check that replace uses, and add an adopt version of `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes`? (The added `test_adopt_updates_setting` only covers a value that differs.) — Adopt mode breaks the module docstring's promise ("Merge settings while preserving untouched configuration files.", app/config.py:1). It reformats user config files that need no change and reports keys that were not adopted to callers.

## Strengths
- The replace branch still writes nothing when the value is unchanged and updates the file when the value differs. I checked this by reading the existing `test_unchanged_replacement_preserves_bytes` and the added `test_replace_updates_different_setting`.
